instructions.objective: Note who comes to the Sleeping Giant twice

order.title: Instruction 2001: The Inn
order.text:
C.,

While you are at the inn, note who stays more than one night, and who comes back. Names if you have them; descriptions if you don't. You needn't hurry. You'll be there a while.

— E.

report.title: Report 2001: The Inn
report.text:
Instruction 2001

I have kept the room at the inn for some nights now. No guest has stayed more than a night, and none has come back. Travellers pass through on the road to Whiterun or Helgen and are not seen again. The regulars are villagers.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2001: The Inn
reply.text:
C.,

Your note on the inn's guests is received. No one stays, and no one comes back. Very well. Keep watching anyway. An inn where nobody lingers is either very dull or very careful, and I should like to know which.

— E.

notYet.text: You have not spent enough nights at the Sleeping Giant to say who comes back. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Learn the proprietor's habits

order.title: Instruction 2002: The Proprietor
order.text:
C.,

The woman who keeps the inn. Her hours, her habits, who she talks to and who she doesn't. Do not ask her anything she would remember being asked.

— E.

report.title: Report 2002: The Proprietor
report.text:
Instruction 2002

The proprietor keeps to the inn. She is up before the cook and seldom far from the bar. She is civil to guests and says little. The cook answers for her and will not discuss her. I have seen no one call on her privately.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2002: The Proprietor
reply.text:
C.,

Received. A proprietor who is always at home and has no callers. How restful for her. You will go on lodging there, and you will go on asking her nothing.

— E.

notYet.text: You have not lodged at the Sleeping Giant long enough to describe the proprietor's habits. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Learn which neighbours pray to the Ninth

order.title: Instruction 2003: Neighbours
order.text:
C.,

Learn which of your neighbours pray to the Ninth, and which only grumble about those who are taken for it. The difference matters more than you'd think.

— E.

report.title: Report 2003: Neighbours
report.text:
Instruction 2003

The miller and his wife speak openly for Ulfric. She has a brother with the Stormcloaks and says the arrests are why. The smith is for the Empire, though he resents the arrests as much as anyone; his nephew is a Legionary. I have seen no shrine in the village. What prayers there are, are said indoors.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2003: Neighbours
reply.text:
C.,

Thank you. A miller for Ulfric and a smith for the Empire, in a village of twenty. Skyrim in miniature. You needn't report on them again unless one of them does something interesting.

— E.

notYet.text: You have not lived in Riverwood long enough to know your neighbours' loyalties. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Hear the street preacher in Whiterun

order.title: Instruction 2004: The Preacher
order.text:
C.,

I'm told there is a priest in Whiterun who preaches Talos in the street, in daylight, under the Jarl's own windows. Go and listen to him once. Note whether the guards do anything about it.

— E.

report.title: Report 2004: The Preacher
report.text:
Instruction 2004

I have been to Whiterun. The priest preaches every day below Dragonsreach, at a statue of Talos, to whoever will stop. The guards pass him without a word. Few stop.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2004: The Preacher
reply.text:
C.,

Received. The guards do nothing and the people do not listen, which is very much what I expected of Whiterun. Leave him alone. A man shouting at a statue is harmless; a man taken away for it is not.

— E.

notYet.text: You have not been to Whiterun yet. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Note which soldiers use the roads

order.title: Instruction 2005: The Roads
order.text:
C.,

When you travel, note which soldiers use the roads, how many, and in what colours. Do not follow them, and do not be followed.

— E.

report.title: Report 2005: The Roads
report.text:
Instruction 2005

Legion patrols use the road from Whiterun south, in threes. I have seen Stormcloaks on the eastern roads, also in threes, and once a fight between them. Our friends pass now and then with a prisoner. Nobody stops them.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2005: The Roads
reply.text:
C.,

Your report on the roads is received, and is about what I expected. Nobody stops our friends. Good. Help keep it that way by not being seen anywhere near them.

— E.

notYet.text: You have not been in Riverwood long enough to describe the roads. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Learn why a friend stopped reporting near Lake Ilinalta

order.title: Instruction 2006: A Silence
order.text:
C.,

One of our friends stopped reporting some weeks ago. He was last occupied with the hills above Lake Ilinalta, south of the standing stones. If you happen to find out why, bring me whatever he was carrying. Don't go looking for trouble on his account; he found enough for both of you.

— E.

report.title: Report 2006: A Silence
report.text:
Instruction 2006

I found him on a promontory in the hills, beside a shrine to Talos, with four of the worshippers. All dead some time. The enclosed letter was on his body.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2006: A Silence
reply.text:
C.,

Your report concerning the man on the hillside has been received, together with a letter of mine I am not in the habit of having returned to me. It appears his informant was reliable after all. That doesn't change the fact that he went up there alone, which I don't recall advising.

The shrine will be attended to. You will say nothing about any of this in Riverwood.

— E.

notYet.text: You have nothing of his to send. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Hire the Dunmer at the Drunken Huntsman

order.title: Instruction 2007: The Dunmer
order.text:
C.,

The Dunmer who drinks at the Drunken Huntsman in Whiterun sells her sword. Hire her before you go west. Accounts will advance her fee on request; it is not to be spent on anything else.

— E.

report.title: Report 2007: The Dunmer
report.text:
Instruction 2007

I have hired the Dunmer from the Drunken Huntsman. Her fee is paid. She asks no questions.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2007: The Dunmer
reply.text:
C.,

You may keep the Dunmer on afterwards, if you find her company agreeable. You'll pay for it yourself, naturally.

— E.

notYet.text: You have not hired the Dunmer yet. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Learn who is killing whom in Markarth

order.title: Instruction 2008: The Killings
order.text:
C.,

Once in Markarth, learn who is killing whom, and on whose account. Begin wherever the city is already bleeding. That will not take you long.

— E.

report.title: Report 2008: The Killings
report.text:
Instruction 2008

The killings in Markarth are the Forsworn's, but the Forsworn take their orders from a prisoner in the city's own silver mine, and the family that owns the mine knows it. The inquiry ended with me in Cidhna Mine.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2008: The Killings
reply.text:
C.,

So the Silver-Bloods keep the king of the Forsworn in their own mine and pay him to murder their rivals. How very Nord. And you were arrested for finding out. I'm told our friend in the Keep was asked about you and could not recall the name. Neither could I.

— E.

notYet.text: You have not yet learned who is behind the killings in Markarth. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Decide the fate of the old man in the mine

order.title: Instruction 2009: The Old Man
order.text:
C.,

If you find yourself in the company of the old man who runs the Forsworn from inside the mine, consider whether the Reach would be livelier with him outside it. I leave the decision to you.

— E.

report.title: Report 2009: The Old Man
report.text:
Instruction 2009

The matter of the old man in the mine is settled. The particulars are set down here.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2009: The Old Man
reply.text:
C.,

I'm told the old man in the mine is loose in the Reach and the Jarl can talk of nothing else. Good. That is very much what I sent you there to do.

— E.

notYet.text: The matter of the old man in the mine is not settled yet. Nothing has been filed.

altReply.title: Reply 2009: The Old Man
altReply.text:
C.,

The Jarl is grateful, I hear. He has pardoned you, and the Silver-Bloods have given you a ring. How very nice for you. I did not send you to Markarth to be thanked by Nords.

— E.

instructions.objective: Learn why the Hall of the Dead was closed

order.title: Instruction 2010: The Hall of the Dead
order.text:
C.,

The Hall of the Dead in Markarth has been closed, and the priest is unpopular for closing it. Find out why. If whoever is responsible proves to be a citizen of some standing, I should like their names more than their heads.

— E.

report.title: Report 2010: The Hall of the Dead
report.text:
Instruction 2010

Those responsible meet in a cave outside the city. They are citizens of Markarth, the butcher among them. I sat at their table. Their names are set down here. The priest will not be reopening the Hall.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2010: The Hall of the Dead
reply.text:
C.,

The names are received, and they are more interesting than I'd hoped. A city whose respectable people eat its dead can be persuaded to do a great many things. You'll say nothing of what you ate, I trust. I certainly won't.

— E.

notYet.text: You have not dealt with the trouble at the Hall of the Dead in a way that leaves you with names. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Help our friend in the Keep with the skald

order.title: Instruction 2011: The Skald
order.text:
C.,

Our friend in the Keep has a skald he suspects of praying to the Ninth, and nothing to prove it with. If he asks you for help, give it. It costs me nothing to oblige him.

— E.

report.title: Report 2011: The Skald
report.text:
Instruction 2011

Our friend in the Keep has the skald's amulet. I found it in the skald's house and took it to him.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2011: The Skald
reply.text:
C.,

I understand our friend in the Keep has his skald at last. He'll be insufferable about it for weeks. Still, it costs the house nothing, and it keeps him occupied.

— E.

notYet.text: Our friend in the Keep does not have the skald's amulet yet. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Find the shrine below Markarth and tell no one

order.title: Instruction 2012: Below the City
order.text:
C.,

There is a shrine to the Ninth somewhere below Markarth that our friend in the Keep has never found. Find it. Tell me, and tell no one else. He in particular is not to hear of it.

— E.

report.title: Report 2012: Below the City
report.text:
Instruction 2012

The shrine is below the city, in use, and tended. I have told no one.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2012: Below the City
reply.text:
C.,

Received. Leave it standing. It does more for us full of angry Nords than it would empty. If our friend in the Keep ever finds it, it will not be because of you.

— E.

notYet.text: You have not found the shrine below Markarth. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Learn what the Jarl's Altmer scholar is working on

order.title: Instruction 2013: The Translator
order.text:
C.,

The Jarl keeps an Altmer scholar in the Keep who translates the Dwemer for him. An Altmer who serves a Nord Jarl. Learn what he is working on, if you can do it without being noticed by him or by our friend.

— E.

report.title: Report 2013: The Translator
report.text:
Instruction 2013

The scholar works in his own rooms in the Keep and in the ruins beneath it. His work is on the Dwemer language. He guards it closely and talks of little else.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2013: The Translator
reply.text:
C.,

Thank you. A Mer who has made himself indispensable to a Nord, and guards his work from everyone. I can't say I blame him. Leave him to it for now.

— E.

notYet.text: You have not been to Understone Keep. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Gain admission to the College of Winterhold

order.title: Instruction 2014: Admission
order.text:
C.,

When the College has admitted you, say so.

— E.

report.title: Report 2014: Admission
report.text:
Instruction 2014

I have been admitted to the College as an apprentice. The adviser keeps his own counsel and sits in on the masters' business uninvited.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2014: Admission
reply.text:
C.,

Received. Remain a student. You will be told when that changes.

— E.

notYet.text: The College has not admitted you yet. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Report what the College finds at Saarthal

order.title: Instruction 2015: The Dig
order.text:
C.,

The College digs at Saarthal. Whatever they find there, I would like to know of it before the adviser tells me.

— E.

report.title: Report 2015: The Dig
report.text:
Instruction 2015

The dig at Saarthal uncovered a sealed chamber and, inside it, a great orb of some kind, now taken back to the College. A monk appeared to me in a vision and warned of danger. I report that because it happened, not because I understand it.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2015: The Dig
reply.text:
C.,

A vision. How very like the College. Describe the object to no one, and do not handle it again.

— E.

notYet.text: Nothing has come of the dig at Saarthal yet. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Follow the College's search through its books

order.title: Instruction 2016: The Books
order.text:
C.,

If the College goes looking in its books for what it found, look with it.

— E.

report.title: Report 2016: The Books
report.text:
Instruction 2016

The librarian sent me after stolen books. One of them, Night of Tears, speaks of Saarthal in the days of the Snow Elves. The College has it back.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2016: The Books
reply.text:
C.,

Thank you. The Snow Elves. I shall read it myself when I have a quiet evening, which is to say not soon.

— E.

notYet.text: The College's search through its books is not finished. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Report the adviser's interest in you

order.title: Instruction 2017: The Adviser's Interest
order.text:
C.,

If the adviser ever takes an interest in you, report it the same day.

— E.

report.title: Report 2017: The Adviser's Interest
report.text:
Instruction 2017

The adviser interrupted my lesson and insisted I speak to a monk of the Psijic Order, who had come to the Arch-Mage's quarters asking for whoever found the orb. He was very eager that I go.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2017: The Adviser's Interest
reply.text:
C.,

You were right to go with him. You were wrong to let him choose your words for you. In future, he gets nothing from you that I haven't seen first.

— E.

notYet.text: The adviser has taken no particular interest in you yet. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Give your account of how the business at the College ends

order.title: Instruction 2018: The End of It
order.text:
C.,

Whatever ends this business at the College, I will want your account of it.

— E.

report.title: Report 2018: The End of It
report.text:
Instruction 2018

The adviser is dead. The orb, the Eye of Magnus they call it, has been taken away by the Psijic monks. The College is rebuilding.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2018: The End of It
reply.text:
C.,

The adviser is dead, I'm told, and the College is calling it an accident of his own making. That is precisely what the house will call it, too.

— E.

notYet.text: The business at the College is not finished. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Send her a book from the Arcanaeum, if it can be done unseen

order.title: Instruction 2019: The Arcanaeum
order.text:
C.,

The College keeps a library (the Arcanaeum, I believe they call it) with a number of volumes the house has never managed to acquire by honest means: on the dragons, chiefly, and on Akavir. Should one of them leave the building without the librarian noticing, I'd be glad to have it. I would rather not hear that you were caught.

— E.

report.title: Report 2019: The Arcanaeum
report.text:
Instruction 2019

A book from the Arcanaeum, enclosed. The librarian has not noticed.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2019: The Arcanaeum
reply.text:
C.,

The book arrived safely. I trust the Orc hasn't noticed yet.

— E.

notYet.text: You have none of the books she asked for. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Learn what Winterhold thinks of the College and its Jarl

order.title: Instruction 2020: Winterhold
order.text:
C.,

While you're there, learn what the town thinks of the College, and of its Jarl. I don't imagine it will take you long.

— E.

report.title: Report 2020: Winterhold
report.text:
Instruction 2020

The town blames the College for the Collapse and the empty houses. The Jarl is for Ulfric, and short of everything but grievances.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2020: Winterhold
reply.text:
C.,

Thank you for your report on Winterhold. It is very much as I expected: a ruin with a Jarl in it. You needn't trouble yourself with the town again.

— E.

notYet.text: You have not spent time in Winterhold's longhouse and inn. Nothing has been filed.

instructions.objective: Take the librarian's reading test

order.title: Instruction 2021: The Librarian's Test
order.text:
C.,

I'm told the librarian sets new students a test on what they read. Take it.

— E.

report.title: Report 2021: The Librarian's Test
report.text:
Instruction 2021

I have been to the librarian about his reading test. How it went is set down here.

— C.

reply.title: Reply 2021: The Librarian's Test
reply.text:
C.,

An Orc, teaching method. Skyrim never stops surprising me. Do take the lesson to heart.

— E.

notYet.text: You have not taken the librarian's test. Nothing has been filed.

altReply.title: Reply 2021: The Librarian's Test
altReply.text:
C.,

I'm told you declined the librarian's test. I had not thought you so short of time.

— E.

letter.title: A Note
letter.text:
C.,

I'm told you've taken a room at the inn and pay for it on time. Good. Keep it that way.

— E.

letter.title: A Letter
letter.text:
C.,

Riverwood has served its purpose, and so, for the moment, have you.

There is a Dunmer who drinks at the Drunken Huntsman in Whiterun who will sell her sword to anyone with the coin. Hire her. Accounts will advance her fee, and I trust you won't mistake it for an allowance. When that's done, go to Markarth. Your instructions for the Reach follow, along with something on the Reach you won't have read. The Forsworn tell it rather differently.

— E.

letter.title: A Letter
letter.text:
C.,

The Reach has been unusually quiet of late, and I find I don't care for it. Our friend in the Keep writes diligent, thorough reports that tell me nothing at all.

You will go to Markarth as what you appear to be, a sellsword in want of work. You'll find the city has no shortage of people at one another's throats. See that they stay there. How you manage it is your own affair; I shall judge you by the state of Markarth when you leave it.

Our friend in the Keep is not to know you are mine. He would only want to help.

Burn this.

— E.

letter.title: A Note
letter.text:
C.,

I have nothing for you at present. Use the time. Your magic is an embarrassment and your history isn't much better, and I'd like both improved before I next have need of you.

— E.

letter.title: A Letter
letter.text:
C.,

You will go to Winterhold and present yourself to the College as a prospective student. Our friends keep an adviser there, whose standing among the masters I would like to understand rather better than his own reports allow. Learn what weight he carries, and who listens to him.

You are a student and nothing more. You will not tell the adviser who sent you. He has no need to know, and I suspect he wouldn't take it well.

Two books accompany this. Read them before you arrive; the masters will assume you have. If you come across anything on the Collapse, read that too.

— E.

letter.title: A Letter
letter.text:
C.,

I have read your report twice. Whatever the adviser believes he is doing at the College, he is not doing it on my authority, and I won't have the house's name attached to it.

You are authorised to see that he does not leave Winterhold. I trust I needn't explain what that means.

Afterwards there will be a great deal of talk, and none of it will be yours.

Burn this.

— E.

letter.title: A Note
letter.text:
C.,

You turned down the Arch-Mage's chair. Good. Everyone watches an Arch-Mage, and you are no use to me watched.

— E.

conditions.plugin: At Your Own Pace - College of Winterhold.esp

letter.title: A Note
letter.text:
C.,

So you're Arch-Mage. I didn't ask for that, and I'll be very interested to learn how you mean to remain useful to me now that every fool in the College is watching you.

— E.

wander.title: A Note
wander.text:
C.,

I understand you were outside Whiterun and Falkreath some days ago. I don't recall giving you leave. Perhaps you'll be good enough to explain what took you there. No, on reflection, don't. Return to Riverwood and stay there.

— E.
